blocks.text: Quick verdict

Decodo is the stronger choice for steady scraping workloads: its 115M+ pool is more than three times IPRoyal's advertised size, it is cheaper at 10 GB ($35 against $52.50), and its published 100 GB price of $275 is easy to budget. IPRoyal is the better pick if your traffic is irregular or seasonal, because its residential gigabytes never expire, and if you run account-based work that benefits from sticky sessions of up to seven days. Teams that may later want parsed results should lean Decodo for its scraping APIs.

Decodo and IPRoyal are the two names most mid-size scraping teams end up choosing between. Decodo, the rebranded Smartproxy, offers a much bigger pool and near-perfect benchmark success rates at a mid-market price. IPRoyal offers a smaller network but some of the most flexible billing in the industry, with residential traffic that never expires and sticky sessions measured in days. Which one is cheaper and better depends heavily on whether your usage is steady or bursty, so this comparison works through both cases.

blocks.text: Decodo in 2026: what you get

Decodo (formerly Smartproxy) sits between the budget brands and the enterprise giants. It gives every customer the full 115M+ residential pool, city and ZIP targeting, and a self-service dashboard that most people can configure in minutes. Proxyway's annual tests ranked its pool second only to Oxylabs in size among the providers it tested, at a price well below enterprise level, which is why Decodo shows up on almost every shortlist.

Strengths: Large 115M+ pool at a mid-market price; Near-perfect success rates in independent tests; Clean, fast self-service onboarding; Scraping APIs available when raw proxies are not enough. Weak spots: Plan traffic does not roll over; Published pricing stops at 100 GB; beyond that you need a quote; More expensive per GB than budget brands.
IPRoyal in 2026: what you get

IPRoyal is a value-focused provider best known for residential traffic that never expires. You can buy a single gigabyte, use it over months, and top up when you need to, which suits irregular projects better than monthly allowances. The residential pool is advertised at 32M+ IPs across 195 countries with state and city targeting, and sticky sessions can be requested for up to seven days. IPRoyal also sells ISP, datacenter and mobile proxies and a Web Unblocker billed per successful request.

Strengths: Residential traffic that does not expire; Sticky sessions up to 7 days; Can start with a single gigabyte; Several proxy types plus Web Unblocker in one account. Weak spots: Smaller pool than the enterprise networks; Headline $1.75/GB rate needs a 10 TB purchase; Mid-volume prices are not published.
Pricing: Decodo vs IPRoyal

Decodo sells residential traffic at $4/GB pay-as-you-go with no commitment, or on monthly plans: 3 GB for $11.25 ($3.75/GB), 10 GB for $35, 25 GB at $3.25/GB, 50 GB for $150 and 100 GB for $275 ($2.75/GB). Top-ups are billed at your plan's rate, so you are not pushed into the next tier.

IPRoyal's residential subscription costs $7 for 1 GB, $11.90 for 2 GB and $52.50 for 10 GB ($5.25/GB); pay-as-you-go is 5% more ($7.35 for 1 GB). The advertised $1.75/GB rate applies only at 10 TB. Prices for custom volumes such as 25, 100 or 500 GB are calculated in the dashboard.

At 10 GB a month, Decodo is the cheaper option at about $35 against $52.50 for IPRoyal, roughly 33% less. At 100 GB, a like-for-like total is harder to state because IPRoyal does not publish an exact price for that volume; Decodo comes to about $275. Look past the per-GB figure too. IPRoyal lets unused traffic carry forward, while Decodo's allowance does not (plan traffic resets monthly; payg for bursty work). For irregular workloads, that difference can outweigh a small gap in list price.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

Decodo has the bigger advertised network, 115M+ residential IPs against 32M+ for IPRoyal, roughly 3.6 times larger. Advertised pool sizes are marketing figures counted over long periods; the number of IPs actually reachable in a given country at a given moment is far smaller for every provider, so treat these as a rough guide to depth rather than a guarantee. For coverage, Decodo lists 195+ countries and IPRoyal lists 195. On targeting, Decodo offers country, state, city, ZIP and ASN, while IPRoyal offers country, state and city (ISP selection needs verification).
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, Decodo offers rotating or sticky sessions with configurable duration, and IPRoyal offers rotating or sticky sessions from 1 second up to 7 days. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: Decodo wins. The deciding factor for Decodo: a large pool and near-perfect benchmark success rates. The limitation on the IPRoyal side: solid success rates and non-expiring traffic for bursty crawls.
SERP and rank tracking: Decodo. Decodo has the edge here. Why: a dedicated SERP scraping API plus city targeting. How IPRoyal compares: it works, but it has no dedicated SERP product.

Social media and multi-account management: IPRoyal wins. The deciding factor for IPRoyal: 7-day sticky sessions keep one IP on one account. The limitation on the Decodo side: sticky sessions, sub-users and an easy dashboard.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. Decodo: ZIP targeting and a ready-made e-commerce API. IPRoyal: city targeting with pay-only-for-what-you-use traffic. Let price and the countries you need decide.

Ad verification and geo-testing: Decodo. Decodo has the edge here. Why: wide coverage with city and ASN targeting. How IPRoyal compares: decent coverage but no ASN or carrier targeting on standard accounts.
Tight budgets: IPRoyal. IPRoyal has the edge here. Why: small entry purchases and traffic that never expires. How Decodo compares: it is mid-priced, not cheap.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. Decodo: Free trial (about 100 MB) on residential. IPRoyal: No general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies. Verification and payment rules differ too. Decodo: Light KYC; checks on some targets. IPRoyal: Optional ID verification; required for ISP-level targeting and PayPal. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test Decodo and IPRoyal before you commit
The quickest way to choose between Decodo and IPRoyal is a side-by-side test on the sites and countries you actually care about:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (Decodo: free trial (about 100 MB) on residential; IPRoyal: no general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.
3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country.
4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, Decodo comes out ahead in 3, IPRoyal in 2, and 1 is a tie. That makes Decodo the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: Decodo is strongest for small and mid-size scraping teams, while IPRoyal is strongest for irregular or seasonal projects. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
